transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My sleep is completely off—I either lie awake most of the night or crash at odd hours and still wake up exhausted. It's just gotten to the point where I feel completely drained all the time, and I really need some help figuring out how to fix it.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, alongside your sleep disturbances?

Yes, I've had this deep, heavy feeling of emptiness and hopelessness for over two years now. I constantly feel worthless, like I'm just a burden to everyone around me, and it's always there right alongside my sleep struggles. It has made it incredibly hard for me to function or do anything anymore.
Can you tell me if your feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, as well as your sleep disturbances, have been constant over the past two years or if they have fluctuated in severity?

They have been incredibly constant, and I can't remember the last time that heavy, hopeless feeling lifted for more than a day or two. While other things might fluctuate slightly, the terrible sleep and this deep exhaustion have been a persistent, daily struggle ever since my breakup.
You mentioned your symptoms started after a breakup; can you tell me more about how your symptoms have related to significant life events or stressors over the past two years?

Everything started a little over two years ago after a painful breakup with my boyfriend and a stressful conflict with my parents about me staying in northern Alabama. The heavy depression, lack of interest, and exhaustion have been there almost constantly since then. The paranoid feelings of being monitored and hearing that male voice actually started several months later and have been coming and going for over a year now.

Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood and energy levels that lasted for at least two months since your symptoms started, or have your symptoms been consistently present without any notable periods of remission?

No, I haven't had any periods of improvement like that at all. The heavy, hopeless feeling and total lack of energy have been consistently there almost every single day for the past two years. Even on the rare occasion I have a slightly better day, it only lasts for a day or two before I sink right back down.
You mentioned having paranoid feelings of being monitored and hearing a male voice; can you tell me more about when these symptoms occur and how often you experience them?

I hear the male voice a few times a week, mostly at night when I'm alone in my apartment. The feeling that my ex and parents are monitoring me through my coworkers started a few months after the breakup and has been coming and going for over a year. It even happened during a stretch last fall when my mood felt relatively neutral and I wasn't feeling quite as depressed.
Do you believe the voice you hear is real, or do you think it might be a product of your own mind?

When it's happening, the voice feels incredibly real and terrifying, and I'll actually get up to check every room in my apartment. Logically, I know there is nobody there, so I suspect it must be a product of my own mind or all this stress. But in the moment, it is really hard to convince myself of that.
When you have these feelings of being monitored, do you think they are based on facts or evidence that you can see or prove, or do they seem more like fears or suspicions that you can't shake?

Logically, I know I can't prove it and that it probably sounds completely paranoid. But the suspicion is so strong that I just can't shake the feeling that my ex and my parents are quietly feeding information about me to people at my job. Even though there's no concrete evidence, it feels very real to me when I'm at work.
When you're experiencing these feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, do the voices or paranoid feelings seem to be directly related to your mood, or do they seem to be separate experiences?

It actually feels like both. On my worst days, the heavy emptiness and worthlessness pile on at the exact same time I'm hearing the voice and feeling paranoid. But they can also be separate, like last fall when my mood felt pretty neutral but I still heard the voice and felt monitored.
Have you ever experienced a period where your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, significantly improved, but the hallucinations or paranoid delusions persisted?

Yes, last fall there was a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt relatively neutral and I didn't feel as sad or drained. Even though the heavy depression lifted during that time, I still kept hearing the male voice at night and remained convinced that my family and my ex were watching me through my coworkers.
Can you describe how the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored relate to each other, and do they ever seem to be triggered by specific events or stressors?

They are closely linked because the male voice I hear actually tells me that I'm being watched and that I'm a burden. They often happen at the same time, particularly when I'm alone in my apartment at night or when my depression is at its worst. They originally started a few months after my breakup and family conflict, and they always seem to flare up when I am feeling highly stressed, empty, or overwhelmed.

Do you think the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored are part of your own thoughts and feelings, or do they seem to be imposed on you from outside, like something is forcing you to think or hear these things?

The male voice sounds like a real, physical person speaking to me from somewhere in the room, which is why I physically get up to check instead of it just feeling like an internal thought. As for the monitoring, it feels like a real external plot being carried out around me, but I don't feel like some outside force is physically forcing thoughts into my head or controlling my mind directly.

Have you ever had a period where the hallucinations or paranoid delusions were the predominant symptoms, and your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, were less prominent or even absent?

Yes, that happened during that stretch last fall I mentioned. For about two weeks, my depressive symptoms were mostly absent and my mood felt relatively neutral, but the male voice at night and the feeling of being monitored were still just as strong.

Can you describe any instances where the male voice you hear provides commentary on your actions or thoughts, or seems to be conversing with you, rather than just making statements about being watched or being a burden?

No, the voice doesn't actually converse with me or comment on what I'm doing. It only ever repeats those specific, scary statements about me being a burden or being watched. It's always just those same repetitive phrases, usually when I'm alone in my apartment at night.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being controlled or influenced by an external force or power?

No, I have never felt like an external force is controlling or influencing my thoughts or actions. Even when I hear the voice or feel paranoid, my thoughts and decisions still feel entirely like my own.
Can you tell me if there are any times when you feel like the male voice is responding to your thoughts or if it seems to know things about you that you haven't told anyone?

No, it doesn't ever respond to my thoughts or reveal any secrets. It just tells me that I'm a burden or that I'm being watched, which still makes me get up and check every room even though I know no one is there.
Have you ever experienced any significant disorganization in your thinking or behavior, such as difficulty maintaining a logical flow of thoughts or engaging in aimless or purposeless activities?

Yes, sometimes at work I'll find myself standing completely frozen in the hallway or by the copier, just staring into space. I feel totally unable to move or figure out what I'm supposed to be doing next until a coworker snaps me out of it.

Can you clarify if the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored are always consistent with your depressive mood, or if there are times when these experiences seem unrelated to how you're feeling emotionally?

While they usually pile on together during my worst depressive periods, there are definitely times when they happen independently of my mood. For instance, during that stretch last fall, my mood felt relatively neutral for about two weeks. Yet, I still heard the male voice at night and felt completely convinced that my family and ex were monitoring me through my coworkers.

Can you tell me if the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored have ever completely stopped for a period of time, say a few weeks or a month, without any treatment or change in your environment?

Yes, they do come and go. There have been periods of a few weeks where the voice and the feeling of being watched seemed to quiet down or stop completely before starting up again. This would happen on its own, even without any treatment or changes in my environment.
Can you describe if the male voice you hear is ever commanding you to do something, or if it's just making statements about being watched or being a burden?

No, the voice never commands me to do anything. It only makes those negative statements telling me that I'm a burden or that I'm being watched. Hearing those things just makes me feel paranoid enough to get up and check all the rooms.
Do you think the male voice and the feelings of being monitored are part of a single problem, or do they seem like separate issues to you?

I definitely feel like they are part of the same problem. The male voice I hear at night actually tells me that I'm being watched, which directly feeds into my belief that my ex and parents are monitoring me through my coworkers. They just feel completely connected to each other.

Have you ever experienced periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep, which might not necessarily be related to your depressive episodes or the male voice and paranoid feelings?

No, I have never experienced periods of high energy or an elevated mood. When I can't sleep, I just wake up feeling exhausted or panicky rather than energized, and my mood is typically low, empty, or neutral. I've never had a time where I felt abnormally high or manic.
Do you think the male voice and your feelings of being monitored could be related to your depression, or do they seem like a separate issue that's not directly connected to your mood?

I think they can be both. While they often pile on together during my worst depressive periods, I've also experienced them separately from my mood. For instance, during a two-week stretch last fall, my mood felt almost neutral, but I still heard the male voice at night and felt convinced my ex and parents were monitoring me through my coworkers.
Have you ever experienced a distinct period where your hallucinations or paranoid delusions were present without any depressive symptoms, lasting for at least two weeks?

Yes, that definitely happened. Last fall, there was a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt relatively neutral and I didn't feel particularly sad or drained. Even so, I still heard the male voice at night and remained convinced that my family and ex were monitoring me through my coworkers.
Can you describe if there was ever a time when the male voice you hear seemed to be in conversation with you, responding to your thoughts or questions, rather than just making statements?

No, the voice has never conversed with me or responded to my thoughts. It only makes one-way statements telling me that I'm a burden or that I'm being watched, especially when I'm alone in my apartment at night. There is never any kind of back-and-forth conversation.

Can you clarify if there have been times when the male voice and feelings of being monitored occurred without any noticeable change in your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness or hopelessness, and if so, how long these periods lasted?

Yes, that happened last fall for about two weeks. During that stretch, my mood felt pretty neutral and I wasn't feeling particularly sad, drained, or worthless, but I still heard the male voice at night and felt convinced my ex and parents were monitoring me through my coworkers.
Have you ever had a period where the hallucinations, such as hearing the male voice, were the primary symptom and lasted for at least a month without significant depressive symptoms?

No, it has never lasted for a full month. Last fall, there was indeed a time when my mood felt relatively neutral and I wasn't feeling particularly sad or drained while still hearing the voice and feeling monitored, but that period only lasted for about two weeks.
Can you think of any times when the male voice or feelings of being monitored seemed to trigger or worsen your depressive symptoms, or if they seemed to be completely separate experiences?

It’s really a mix of both. On my worst days, everything piles on at once and hearing the voice or feeling monitored definitely makes my feelings of emptiness and worthlessness feel much heavier. However, they also occur separately, like last fall when my mood felt relatively neutral for a couple of weeks, yet I still heard the male voice and felt convinced I was being watched at work.
Have you ever experienced a period where the hallucinations or paranoid delusions were present for at least a month without any depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness or hopelessness?

No, it has never lasted for a full month. Last fall, there was a period of about two weeks where my mood felt relatively neutral and I didn't feel depressed or worthless, but I still heard the male voice at night and believed my family and ex were monitoring me through my coworkers.
Can you tell me if there has ever been a time when the male voice and feelings of being monitored completely stopped for a period, but your feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness persisted?

Yes, even when the voice and the feeling of being watched quiet down or temporarily stop, the deep sadness, hopelessness, and lack of motivation never really go away. I honestly can't remember the last time I actually felt like myself or enjoyed anything for more than a day or two, even during those quieter times.
